In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the disk M dwarf population is not a simple power-law function of mass.
the disk M dwarf mass function is not a power law but a function of metallicity.
the M dwarf luminosity and mass functions are flat and that the disk scale length is short.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the local surface density of M dwarfs is 13.0 ± 1.5 M☉ pc -2 and the disk scale length is 2.8 ± 0.2 kpc.
the disk parameters derived from the M dwarf luminosity/mass function are consistent with the results obtained using other tracers, such as K and M giants.
the disk scale height is about 300 pc and the disk scale length is about 3 kpc, with an uncertainty of about 30% on each parameter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the disk M dwarf luminosity and mass functions are not universal but depend on the height above the plane.
the M dwarf luminosity functions derived using local relations and height-dependent relations are similar, but the mass functions obtained using the two approaches are quite different.
the disk scale length of M dwarfs is not as sensitive to the choice of the relations used as the peak value of the luminosity function.
